newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra share row engulfs two more ministers.
newsitem.headline: Canberra share row engulfs two more ministers.

text.p: The Australian opposition will add Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer and Finance Minister John Fahey to its list of targets in the intensifying share ownership row, according to media reports on Wednesday.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported that Fischer, who is also trade minister, appeared to be in breach of ministerial guidelines, but had "quietly sold off" shares in major mining and exporting companies over the last few months.
He had also divested some shares since the start of the so-called "share affair" last week, the newspaper reported.
Under Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines, government members are required to divest any investment interests which may conflict with their portfolio area.

"A spokesman for Mr Fischer confirmed last night that the minister has been selling off his share portfolio for a number of months, but admitted some of these sales had occurred in the past few days," the newspaper said.
The newspaper also said Fahey would come under attack because of his failure to declare ownership of some shares in the pecuniary interest register for members of parliament.
Fischer and Fahey were both unavailable for comment on Wednesday.

The share row has already claimed two scalps with the resignation of Assistant Treasurer Jim Short on Sunday, followed on Tuesday by the resignation of Senator Brian Gibson as Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer.
Both men resigned because of decisions they had made regarding companies in which they held shares.
Industry Minister John Moore has also come under fire, but Moore has said there is no conflict of interest as he is trying to sell the shares he holds in a venture capital company.
